findings.evidence: Grep hits: lines 89, 96, and 115 define the pointwise laws without `@[simp]`; analogous quotient API marks `elementaryTwoQuotientCongr_refl_apply` and `elementaryTwoQuotientCongr_trans_apply` as `@[simp]` at `TauCeti/Algebra/Group/ElementaryTwoQuotient/Basic.lean:251,256` and the class-group wrapper at `TauCeti/NumberTheory/ClassGroup/ElementaryTwoQuotient.lean:144,149`.
findings.fix: Mark these pointwise forms `@[simp]` (renaming `mulEquiv_symm_apply'` if needed to avoid the generated Mathlib name) or provide equivalently named `@[simp]` normal-form wrappers.
findings.issue: The public pointwise characteristic laws `mulEquiv_trans_apply`, `mulEquiv_refl_apply`, and `mulEquiv_symm_apply'` are deliberately not `@[simp]`, so normal class-group action expressions are not exposed as simplifier normal forms.

findings.evidence: Line 123 declares `@[expose] noncomputable def mulEquivHom`; line 129 provides the intended computation lemma `@[simp] theorem mulEquivHom_apply ... := rfl`, so exposing the definition body is unnecessary public surface.
findings.fix: Remove `@[expose]` from `mulEquivHom` and keep/extend characteristic lemmas such as `mulEquivHom_apply` and pointwise simp forms for computation.
findings.issue: `mulEquivHom` exposes its body even though the public API already supplies `mulEquivHom_apply`; downstream consumers should not need to unfold the bundled hom to use the action.

summary: The public surface still exposes implementation details and withholds automation from the pointwise functorial normal forms consumers need for class-group actions.
